# Functional, transport, and localization retrospective

This is a strategy memo, not a new OC theorem. It deliberately stops the
current omitted-index/tilt calculation. I reviewed the recent registry,
the dominated-centroid and multiple-pair sources, their seven-fiber and
all-template obstructions, the simultaneous-localization obstruction,
and the selected-circuit/contact-rigidity sources.

## 1. Where the actual connection to integer geometry remains

The strongest portable continuous input is currently the dominated
centroid theorem, together with the conditional triangular coupling.
These accept arbitrary convex endpoint shapes, put their output in an
ACTUAL integer midpoint fiber, and control every oblique cap using one
coupling. They therefore already contain the essential geometric link
which the simplex/exponential program still lacks.

The weakness is not its constant alone. The seven-fiber obstruction
defeats even an optimally sharp theorem that remembers only total
midpoint mass and one total density ceiling at its prescribed centroid.
The all-template crossed-box obstruction independently defeats replacing
that lost information by a single optimally chosen common template.
Improving either scalar theorem in isolation will not repair those
certificates.

The ordinary joint-row work is much closer to a genuine multi-direction
statement than separate cap estimates. Its exact triangle results,
six-sector PSD reductions, and local arbitrary-body theorem retain one
actual body and several actual sections. But a proof for arbitrary
ordinary bodies would still need an explicit interface to a SELECTED
mixed critical circuit and the integer witness budget. That interface
must be written before treating a new ordinary inequality as progress
toward OC.

The simplex/exponential identities have supplied substantial mathematics:
all-dimensional cap entropy, both positive omissions with two positive
phases, paired-pattern section products, and exact first moments. Yet
none currently chooses an integer base, combines different fiber shapes,
or reduces the number of charged witness groups to 2^n. The actual
convex-order counterexample shows why mass and barycenter conservation
alone cannot supply that bridge. Completing the remaining variance
omissions might finish an ordinary capacity subprogram; it would not by
itself remove this missing interface.

Localization is presently a tool for a CHOSEN scalar objective, not a
license to replace all fibers by needles. The archived three-fiber
triangle example rules out preserving even three prescribed deficient
cap inequalities on needles. Any new localization proposal must say
which inequalities it abandons and why the optimizing certificate still
survives. Preserving all fiber masses and all active caps by declaration
is already falsified.

**Recommendation:** park further variance omissions and tilt optimization
after saving/auditing the completed results. Reopen them only when a
specific mixed certificate has a proved reduction to their exact
hypotheses. At present the arithmetic selected-circuit/transport bridge
has higher strategic value than another section-product family.

## 2. Synthesis A: barycentric hyperedges with their actual cap surplus

The midpoint program can be enlarged without assuming a common shape or
a common reflection center. Fix an actual integer anchor p. Use finite
hyperedges E of measured bases z with positive weights lambda_z summing
to one and sum lambda_z z=p. These include noncollinear integer
barycentric relations which no reflected-pair star sees.

The first exact lemma to prove from the existing conditional-Fubini
construction is the following multi-input version. For convex fibers
K_z of volumes v_z, there is a simultaneous coupling of their uniform
probabilities whose weighted barycenter Z lies in K_p and has density

    density(Z) <= [sum_(z in E) lambda_z v_z^(1/d)]^(-d).       (A1)

One should prove this directly with a common triangular reference map:
the positive diagonal derivatives have fixed determinant v_z, and the
determinant of their weighted diagonal sum satisfies the elementary
Minkowski determinant inequality. Repeated one-dimensional substitution
then gives (A1), without unproved cross-coordinate differentiability.
This is a bounded constructive lemma, not an allocation assertion.

For any ambient halfspace H, its affine threshold identity gives the
exact pointwise inequality

    1_H(p,Z) <= sum_(z in E) 1_H(z,X_z).                     (A2)

If hyperedge E carries mass t_E and each source satisfies
sum_(E containing z) t_E<=v_z, these inequalities can be summed without
reusing source mass. Keep both the actual output measures and the
nonnegative SURPLUS in (A2); do not immediately replace them by the
single scalar ceiling L. Their barycenters and supports are actual,
and every proposed center still lies in K_p.

The novelty worth testing is hyperedge coverage plus retained cap
surplus, not merely inserting another density constant into the old
star envelope. A first falsifier is the actual seven-fiber example,
followed by the crossed-box all-template example. If the enlarged
certificate still fails there even with exact component measures, do
not start a general existence theorem. Sharp binary products must
continue to be paid by the own-fiber option: they have no nontrivial
integer barycentric relation anchored at a vertex.

The unproved arithmetic obligation is explicit: select an anchor and
source-disjoint fractional hyperedges which pay the ORIGINAL mass.
There is no claim that (A1)--(A2) establish it. This route is attractive
because its next objects already contain the lattice and the real
continuous fibers, rather than hoping to restore them later.

## 3. Synthesis B: trade density cost for selected-menu cap surplus

The fixed density ceiling discards a particularly concrete resource:
when both endpoints of a pair lie in a tested cap, the midpoint union
bound has a whole unit of slack. This can be retained for a selected
critical menu instead of demanding that each prescribed profile pay
Gamma on its own.

Here is an exact first lemma, with no conjectural geometric hypothesis.
For a pair of fibers A,B with volumes a,b and a fixed midpoint anchor,
mix a mass-t optimal-density triangular coupling with weight 1-epsilon
and an independent uniform coupling with weight epsilon. Put

    Bstar=((a^(1/d)+b^(1/d))/2)^d.

The output midpoint density is at most

    t[(1-epsilon)/Bstar+epsilon*2^d/max(a,b)].               (B1)

Indeed the independent midpoint density at x is
2^d|A intersect(2x-B)|/(ab). For any finite cap menu H_l with weights
theta_l>=0, sum theta_l=1, its average source-minus-midpoint captured
mass has the additional lower bound

    epsilon*t*sum_l theta_l
           (|A intersect H_(l,A)|/a)(|B intersect H_(l,B)|/b). (B2)

Both-captured pairs prove (B2) directly, and every other pointwise slack
is nonnegative. The same coupling is used for the entire menu.

The archive already retains unused-cap slack in a directional transport
identity. The new proposed object here is its simultaneous selected-menu
budget under a controlled change of the coupling, including the explicit
density cost; the nonnegative union-bound slack itself is not new.

The next task should compare the infinitesimal cost in (B1) with the
gain in (B2) under the ACTUAL critical-response weights, retaining all
source allocation constraints and the selected circuit. One may also
randomize only selected transport cells to avoid paying the full
independence ceiling. This is where ordinary joint-row information
could enter: it constrains several real cap fractions simultaneously,
instead of being promoted to a theorem about unrelated fibers.

There is no universal favorable sign in this memo. Aligned simplex
products are the first sharp test; the R4 strict-quota product is the
first test of the quantifiers. Its bad prescribed profile must not be
mistaken for the absence of a paying selected profile. If the density
cost dominates even for every admissible local randomization, record
that exact failure rather than replacing it with an unproved rounding
or allocation principle.

## 4. A third, lower-priority synthesis: absorption of locked contacts

The contact-rigidity theorem offers a different discrete object. At a
nonexposed high-profile lifted vertex of a common-normal simplex family,
choose one of its proved anchored Jensen-equality representations.
For a fixed vertex type this defines a finite martingale on the ACTUAL
integer bases and lifted vertices.

Its first exact lemma is elementary but useful: a closed recurrent
class cannot contain two distinct bases. Every coordinate of the base
is harmonic in a finite irreducible class and therefore constant.
After collapsing trivial classes, the process is absorbed at vertices
with no chosen nontrivial contact relation. Both the integer base and
the lifted vertex coordinates are conserved in the absorption law.
Simultaneous support equalities are propagated, not guessed from
separate facet relations.

This turns the local rigidity statement into an absorbing transport
system with exposed terminal vertices. Its communicating-class quotient
is a DAG; individual transient classes may have cycles. A possible new
invariant is the total
COAREA-WEIGHTED terminal charge for a favorably selected circuit, with
Brunn--Minkowski surplus charged where the affine contact relations
break. The R4 product is an immediate falsifier of any unweighted
terminal-hit claim: exposure/absorption alone does not pay Gamma.
Accordingly this is secondary until the exact coarea mass balance is
written. It should not replace the current actual normal-bundle
optimization by an abstract graph argument.

## 5. Out-of-box reformulation: optimize a surplus flow, not a center formula

The midpoint and selected-circuit programs can be recast as a finite
source-capacity network whose edges are actual barycentric transports.
Its variables are couplings and source budgets; its observable is the
vector of cap surpluses for a finite critical menu. Centers appear only
as barycenters of actual measures in a chosen target fiber. Integer
geometry constrains allowable target anchors and barycentric relations.

This is different from a universal scalar inequality for a density, a
distribution over candidate centers, or a claim that every prescribed
circuit pays. The first exact test is finite and reviewable: on one
known obstruction, retain the actual transport output and compute the
entire surplus vector before compressing anything to a total ceiling.
Then dualize that finite menu with the already proved response LP.
The dual should reveal WHICH cross-fiber information is missing, rather
than producing another equivalent-to-OC allocation lemma by definition.

The largest risk is that one target fiber remains insufficient, as in
some archived scalar certificates. If so, the next extension must
prove a deterministic anchor-selection rule from the full budget; an
average over anchors does not count. The factor 2^n must enter at this
discrete selection step. It has no reason to emerge from further
ordinary simplex variance calculations alone.

## 6. Suggested immediate order

1. Finish audits and archive the new variance/tilt theorems; stop their
   unsupported promotion toward general fibers.
2. Prove (A1) and retain (A2)'s exact surplus, then test the existing
   seven-fiber obstruction with that richer data.
3. Analyze the density-cost/surplus trade (B1)--(B2) for one actual
   selected critical menu, including an equality calibration.
4. Return to localization only after the resulting objective and the
   precise finite constraints to preserve are known.

These are proposals for bounded next work after the root synthesis.
None is asserted to provide a complete arbitrary-n,d proof.
